title: throughput-sentinel-adaptive-batching-recommendation-pipeline
creator: Aisha Kumar
description:
Goal: Build an end-to-end recommendation pipeline (Throughput Sentinel) that profiles production workloads, synthesizes lightweight heuristics and ML signals, and emits safe batching and KV-cache configuration changes with automated canary apply and rollback. The pipeline should: 1) produce per-route and per-model batch/caching suggestions that optimize cost (tokens/sec and $/token) while meeting latency SLOs, 2) validate proposals with shadow simulation and short canary windows, 3) support automated rollback and operator override, and 4) surface clear rationale and confidence scores in the Console.

Scope: profiling service offline and nearline; heuristic engine (cost vs latency tradeoffs); a continuous-tuning controller that proposes incremental config deltas (batch size, target latency, KV cache policy, max-concat); a safe-apply orchestrator (canary rollout, telemetry gates, rollback triggers); Console UI hooks for review and manual apply.

Non-goals: end-to-end ML model for parameter prediction (we will use heuristic+lightweight models in later phases), rewriting serving runtime kernels (we rely on existing runtime APIs).
acceptance_criteria: Profiling pipeline ingests 7 days of route-level traces and produces workload fingerprints (seq-length distribution, arrival pattern, token-rate).
Recommendation engine outputs batch and cache suggestions with a confidence score and estimated cost delta for 90% of top-100 routes by volume.
Automated canary apply: canary runs on 2% traffic for configurable window (default 15m) and can auto-rollback if p95 latency regresses > 10% or error rate increases > 2x.
Console shows proposed delta, expected cost change, rationale, and link to simulation shard results.
Safety: every automated apply is reversible and creates a rollback ticket when triggered.
design_decisions: Use a hybrid heuristic+lightweight-gradient model to combine human-readable rules with data-driven corrections (favors explainability for operator trust).
Profile aggregation resolution: 1m windows aggregated to route-level percentiles (p50/p90/p95 seq length and inter-arrival).
Cost estimate model: tokenized input + projected tokens/sec * runtime cost per GPU-second, conservative headroom factor 1.15 for production recommendations.
tradeoffs: Conservative applies reduce cost upside but minimize customer-facing latency regressions.
Short canary windows increase rollout speed but can miss spike-driven regressions; mitigated with post-canary monitoring and extended observation policy for critical routes.
Favor route-level proposals first (simpler rollback surface) vs. cluster-wide blanket tuning.
implementation_plan: M1: Profiling service - collector, aggregation, fingerprinting (2 wks)
M2: Heuristic engine - ruleset authoring, cost model, confidence scoring (2 wks)
M3: Simulation harness - shadow traffic replayer and cost/latency estimator (2 wks)
M4: Safe-apply orchestrator - canary, metric gates, rollback automation (3 wks)
M5: Console integration - UI for proposal review and manual apply (1 wk)
M6: Beta rollout to dedicated customers and monitoring (2 wks)
metrics_and_observability: Primary: p50/p95 latency, tokens/sec, requests/sec, GPU utilization, cost-per-token (estimated)
Safety gates: error-rate, timeouts, OOM events, tail-latency regressions
Experiment dashboards: per-canary time series, compare baseline vs candidate, annotated with canary windows and triggers
testing_plan: Unit tests for heuristic rules and cost model
Integration tests simulating synthetic arrival patterns (bursty, Poisson, steady) and verifying recommendation stability
Shadow-run simulations against last 7 days of traffic for top 200 routes
Canary e2e runs in staging with metric gate automation validated via fault injection
open_questions: How aggressive should auto-apply be for enterprise customers with stricter SLAs? (opt-in by default)
What is the acceptable confidence threshold for fully automatic applies vs manual review?
Do we expose recommendation provenance (which rule or signal produced the suggestion) or only a summary?

2026-02-20 — Profiling prototype demoed: basic fingerprinting implemented; initial workload clusters show bimodal seq-length distribution on /chat endpoints. Link: https://confluence.redwood.ai/x/BatchingProfilingDemo

2026-02-24 — Heuristic draft: added 'latency-first' and 'cost-first' rule families; discussed headroom multiplier tradeoffs with runtime leads. See design doc: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/Batching-Design

2026-02-27 — Simulation results: shadow-run on 3 routes showed cost down 12% with p95 latency +6%; need to tune confidence filter to avoid p95 increase above 5% for customer-impact=high routes. Experiment dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/abcd123/batching-simulations

2026-02-28 — Orchestrator prototype: canary controller implemented; default canary policy 2% traffic, 15m window, gates wired to p95 and error-rate. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/5231
2026-03-01 — Blocker: missing automated rollback hook for Dedicated clusters with pinned capacity; blocking canary auto-apply. Owner: infra (assigned to Priya Nair).
Action items: 1) Add deterministic rollback API for Dedicated (infra), 2) Tune confidence scoring to suppress recommendations for high-impact routes, 3) Build Console review page for beta users.
